arguments.summary: Latest normalized SEC facts establish reported six-/nine-month operating performance, while primary earnings materials with guidance/demand disclosures were retrieved only for NVDA and an index-level Meta 8-K cover item. ANET and MU primary filings were not read within this task; catalysts/guidance and company-specific risks therefore remain unverified for those names. QQQ’s dated holdings show material NVDA/MU/META look-through concentration but are marked stale.

claims.text: ANET reported $5.7447bn revenue, $2.5358bn operating income, $2.2358bn net income and $2.7765bn operating cash flow for the six months ended June 30, 2026; the normalized filing-derived operating and net margins were 44.14% and 38.92%.

MU reported $78.959bn revenue, $55.589bn operating income, $47.268bn net income, $45.702bn operating cash flow and $19.602bn capital expenditure for the nine months ended May 28, 2026; period length differs from the other issuers.

META reported $117.111bn revenue, $41.647bn operating income, $42.621bn net income, $64.088bn operating cash flow and $49.113bn capital expenditure for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Its reported long-term debt was $83.664bn at period-end.

NVDA’s Q2 FY2027 primary release reported quarterly revenue of $96.221bn (+18% quarter-over-quarter, +106% year-over-year), Data Center revenue of $89.0bn (+18% QoQ, +117% YoY), 75.0% GAAP gross margin and $2.46 GAAP diluted EPS. It guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0bn plus or minus 2%, explicitly assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China.

NVDA’s Q2 FY2027 release states Vera Rubin is in full production and reports approximately $99bn remaining under its share-repurchase authorization at quarter-end. The same release identifies the China exclusion in outlook as a disclosed demand/geographic constraint.

QQQ’s sponsor profile dated August 31, 2026 reported 103 holdings and a 30.08 aggregate P/E; the sponsor holdings table dated September 12 lists NVDA at 8.45%, MU at 4.85% and META at 3.07%, with top-10 holdings totaling 47.17%. The holdings table is designated stale and reports 100.05% total weight, so it is dated look-through rather than current exposure.

For the 21/63-session horizon, NVDA’s explicit next-quarter outlook and production-ramp disclosures provide identifiable company reporting catalysts; realization is sensitive to the stated China exclusion and to delivery/ramp execution, rather than being a calibrated forecast.

META’s large reported first-half capital expenditure relative to operating cash flow makes subsequent reporting on AI investment monetization and spending trajectory material to the 21/63-session thesis; the supplied 8-K confirms results were released but its excerpt does not contain the attached earnings release or guidance.

gaps.description: Latest ANET 10-Q/earnings release was identified but not read; no verified quarter-over-quarter trend, guidance, customer/demand concentration, supply constraints, or updated company-specific risks are available in the evidence used here.

Latest MU 10-Q and post-quarter 8-K were identified but not read; no verified quarterly trend, pricing/supply commentary, guidance, inventory/capex plans, or company-specific risks are available in the evidence used here.

META’s supplied 8-K excerpt only identifies an attached results release; it does not provide its guidance, segment/demand discussion, or risk disclosures. A primary earnings exhibit or latest 10-Q detail is needed for catalyst-level conclusions.
QQQ holdings are dated September 12, 2026 but flagged stale; composition may have changed, and ANET is not shown in the listed table, so no claim of zero ANET exposure is supported.
No market-derived valuation multiple, consensus estimates, or verified forward earnings assumptions are supplied for ANET, MU, META or NVDA; no company scenario valuation was performed.

assumptions: Reported filing periods are not directly comparable across issuers (ANET/META six months; MU nine months; NVDA six months).
QQQ holdings are treated solely as dated fund composition, not as any investor’s portfolio allocation.
Any 21/63-session catalyst discussion is conditional on future company disclosures and execution, not a price forecast.
arguments.counter_thesis: Recent reported profitability does not establish forward durability. For NVDA, the disclosed China exclusion, production-ramp execution and elevated Data Center dependence could cause results to differ from the stated outlook. For META, high reported capital expenditure could pressure cash conversion if monetization or advertising demand underperforms. ANET and MU lack read primary materials in this task, preventing an evidence-based counter-case beyond that missingness.

review_conditions.description: Review ANET and MU after reading their latest primary quarterly filings/earnings releases for guidance, demand/supply constraints, concentration and risk-factor changes.

Review META’s attached July 29 earnings release or latest 10-Q detail for guidance, AI spending and monetization disclosures; review NVDA at its next results for delivery against Q3 outlook and whether China Data Center compute assumptions change.
Refresh QQQ sponsor holdings before relying on look-through weights because the September 12 table is marked stale.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Dated QQQ composition embeds material look-through to NVDA, MU and META (8.45%, 4.85%, and 3.07%, respectively), linking the fund to their company-specific results and semiconductor/AI-infrastructure conditions.
shared_exposures.qualification: September 12 sponsor table is marked stale; weights are fund composition, not personalized portfolio exposure, and weights may have changed.
